english.title: Vote in assembly constituency or to fill vacancy for London mayor when proxy appointed to vote elsewhere
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were guilty of an illegal practice in that you voted as an elector otherwise than by proxy in a London Assembly constituency, namely **(..SPECIFY CONSTITUENCY..), at an

(A)_[ordinary election]_
(B)_[election of the Mayor of London to fill a vacancy held under section 16 of the Greater London Authority Act 1999]_

when there was in force an appointment of a person, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), to vote as your proxy at the election in another Assembly constituency, namely **(..SPECIFY OTHER CONSTITUENCY..)
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 61(2A)(e) and (7) and 169 of the Representation of the People Act 1983.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
votes as an elector otherwise than by proxy in an Assembly constituency at an ordinary election
or an election of the Mayor of London held under section 16 of the 1999 Act

english.notes:
61(7) An offence under this section shall be an illegal practice but -
(a) the court before whom a person is convicted of any such offence may, if they think it just in the special circumstances of the case, mitigate or entirely remit any incapacity imposed by virtue of section 173; and (b) a candidate shall not be liable, nor shall his election be avoided, for an illegal practice under this section of any agent of his other than an offence under subsection (5) above.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see section 176

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
